about-app-image-text: With all this programming, I haven't had time to paint lately!
about-app-text-1: In 2021, I started developing an app for playing <link>RMSS</link> for my own use, as a tool to streamline games. When the app was already quite far along, one afternoon whilst looking at my phone I discovered that a new version of Rolemaster was about to be released.
about-app-text-2: So I thought: it’s a bit of a cheek that, after two decades without any new content, they’ve had to release a version right now, just when I’d almost got all the features I wanted!!!
about-app-text-3: Then, during the 2025 holidays, I said to myself, Right, let’s start again, this time by creating a helper tool for the new system.
about-before-text-1: When I was very young, I started using spreadsheets to speed up games and create characters, because whilst doing it with pen and paper has its charm, it ends up being very time-consuming.
about-before-text-2: So, without any knowledge of programming, I began automating certain tasks, mainly the damage tables, so I wouldn’t have to keep looking up the row and column for the Arms Law of the time And those were my first steps in programming, a profession I’ve been working in for 20 years.
about-intro-1: I’m someone who discovered Rolemaster and MERP in the early 90s and, after many years without playing, a bit of a midlife crisis has brought me back to this beloved game.
about-intro-2: Now, 25 years on from those games I used to play with my brother, we’ve got together again to move around Lord of the Rings miniatures, eat pizza and roll the dice.
about-motivation-image-text: Amon Sûl surrounded by buildings? What happened?
about-motivation-text-1: Although I used to play narrative campaigns as a child, the main focus of these was the combat, where you’d end up using miniatures as if it were a small-scale wargame. I’ve always enjoyed these games and have played quite a few of them, mainly 40k.
about-motivation-text-2: I liked gang management games in the style of Necromunda, where you had a small group of characters and simply faced off against another gang.
about-motivation-text-3: And I thought, this style of play, set in Middle-earth – which is by far the setting I’ve always liked best – using Rolemaster rules could work quite well.
about-now-text-1: Now, after many years without playing and having passed my forties, I wanted to recapture those afternoons spent rolling open-ended dices and feel once more what it’s like when a level-one goblin has to roll the dice on the critical hit table.
about-now-text-2: Many of the adventures I prepared back then, with extensive maps and plenty of storytelling, ended with the main character sadly bleeding to death in the mud of a meadow after an encounter on the encounter table with a wild boar and her piglets.
about-now-text-3: That was one of the things I liked most about Rolemaster, its system suited less epic scenarios far better than other 80s role-playing games.
about-testing-text-1: After a few months of development, I finally enlisted my brother to test whether the project was actually feasible, or whether running a game with so many characters and rules would prove too complicated.
about-testing-text-2: The idea was to use a tablet next to the table to work out movements, attacks, manoeuvres… whilst rolling the dice and taking measurements, checking the lines of sight on the table to see what cover an archer’s target would have…
about-testing-text-3: And after several games, I’m happy with the result and I think it’s possible to combine the world of miniature skirmishes with the depth of rules that Rolemaster brings

combat-rule-absolute-hit: The total went past the top of the table: the critical roll gets one point for every five beyond it.
combat-rule-action-points: An attack done with fewer action points than its most: a penalty for each one missing.
combat-rule-ambush: An attack from ambush: the Ambush skill adds to the critical.
combat-rule-attack-number: Several attacks in one action (a kata): a penalty for each attack beyond the first.
combat-rule-attack-size: The attack size multiplies the damage of the table (Hit Multiplier) and raises the critical one level for each size above Medium (or lowers it for each size below), minus the critical size of the target.
combat-rule-attack-targets: The action's attacks aim at more than one foe: a penalty for each foe beyond the first.
combat-rule-bd: The target's defensive bonus (Quickness and other permanent DB). It is lost when the target is unaware of the attack or in frenzy.
combat-rule-binding-chain: Binding Chain: the attack to bind the foe has a penalty.
combat-rule-bo: The attacker's offensive bonus with this attack: the weapon skill and what the sheet adds to it.
combat-rule-called-shot: A called shot at a location: a penalty, in exchange for choosing where the hit lands.
combat-rule-cover: The target is behind cover: a penalty to hit it, twice as large with hard cover.
combat-rule-custom-bonus: A bonus or penalty entered by hand when declaring the attack.
combat-rule-disarm: Disarm: a penalty that depends on the attack table, larger for ranged attacks. The total is read in the bands of the disarm table, not in the attack table.
combat-rule-disarm-defense: The defender opposes the disarm: 100 less the total of its roll ({{defenseRoll}}).
combat-rule-disarm-skill: The Disarm skill ({{skill}}) offsets the penalties of the maneuver ({{penalty}}), never beyond them.
combat-rule-disarm-two-handed: The foe wields a two-handed weapon: harder to knock away.
combat-rule-dodge: The declared dodge: the Running ranks when passive (up to +50), half the skill when partial and all of it when full. Armour and load reduce all of them, injuries the partial and full ones, and against a ranged attack it is halved.
combat-rule-evade-shield: Evade Shield: half of what the target's shield adds is ignored.
combat-rule-flatfooted-rear: In melee a flatfooted target is also attacked as if from the rear, whatever the declared position.
combat-rule-flatfooted-target: The target is flatfooted: it does not see the attack coming. The attacker gets the surprise bonus, and the target loses its DB, shield and dodge.
combat-rule-frenzy-strength: In frenzy the attacker's Strength bonus goes up, once for each time Strength is in the attack's bonus.
combat-rule-game-lethality: The lethality chosen for the game, added to every attack.
combat-rule-graceful-gait: Graceful Gait: the attacker moves without the pace penalty.
combat-rule-heedless-fury: The target fights with Heedless Fury and neglects its defence: a bonus to hit it.
combat-rule-higher-ground: The attacker fights from higher ground: a bonus.
combat-rule-improved-parry: The Improved Parry ability of the target's fighting style adds half the parry.
combat-rule-killing-strike: Killing Strike: a penalty to hit, in exchange for a more severe critical.
combat-rule-killing-strike-target: The target used Killing Strike this round, and opened its guard: a bonus to hit it.
combat-rule-light-weapon: Light weapons make a kata easier: a bonus that offsets its penalties.
combat-rule-melee-cover: Firing into a melee: the other combatants engaged with the target give it partial hard cover, unless the game master declared a cover. A miss may hit one of them.
combat-rule-multiple-attacks-skill: The Multiple Attacks skill offsets the penalties of the kata, never turning them into a bonus.
combat-rule-non-violent: Non-Violent: once the actor has inflicted a critical, its attacks get a penalty for the rest of the combat.
combat-rule-off-hand-dagger: A style ability that removes the off-hand penalty that the sheet puts in this attack's OB.
combat-rule-off-hand-light-weapon: A style ability that removes the off-hand penalty that the sheet puts in this attack's OB.
combat-rule-pace-penalty: The attacker moves this round (by hand, or a free movement during the attack): the faster the pace, the larger the penalty.
combat-rule-pace-penalty-skill: The Footwork skill offsets the pace penalty of melee and thrown attacks, up to its size.
combat-rule-parry: The defender gives part of the OB of its melee attack to parry: each point given is taken off this attack, and its own attacks keep less OB for the rest of the round. It can parry if its last action with AP is a melee attack, and its penalties lower the most it can give.
combat-rule-parry-positional: Parrying an attacker on the flank (-30) or rear (-70), here {{position}}: {{penalty}} to the parry, offset point for point by Reverse Strike ({{skill}}); it never takes off more than the parry ({{parry}}).
combat-rule-penalty-critical: The attacker's penalties from the criticals it has taken.
combat-rule-penalty-endurance: The attacker's penalty for its spent endurance.
combat-rule-penalty-fortitude: Fortitude takes off part of the other penalties.
combat-rule-penalty-hp: The attacker's penalty for the hit points it has lost.
combat-rule-penalty-injury: The attacker's penalties from its injuries.
combat-rule-penalty-non-violent: Non-Violent: the attacker's penalty after inflicting a critical.
combat-rule-penalty-stunned: The attacker is stunned: a penalty.
combat-rule-point-blank-shot: Point-Blank Shot: a bonus against a close target.
combat-rule-positional-source: The attacker strikes toward its own flank or rear: a penalty, twice the positional bonus.
combat-rule-positional-target: Attacking the target in melee from its flank or its rear: a bonus, larger from the rear. The target's shield does not cover these attacks.
combat-rule-positional-target-skill: The target turns to meet the attack: half its Reverse Strike ({{skill}}), divided among the {{foes}} foes attacking it this round, offsets the positional bonus (+{{bonus}}), never by more than the bonus.
combat-rule-pressing-advantage: The attacker inflicted a critical on this foe: its next attack against it gets a bonus.
combat-rule-prone-source: The attacker is on the ground: a large penalty.
combat-rule-prone-target: The target is on the ground: easier to hit in melee, harder at range.
combat-rule-protect: A protector parries for someone else with the OB of its melee attack. Where it stands costs a penalty, which its Protect skill offsets and which it pays when it protects with any amount.
combat-rule-range-in-melee: Shooting or throwing while engaged in melee: a penalty.
combat-rule-range-penalty: Ranged attack: the farther the target, measured in range increments of the weapon, the larger the penalty.
combat-rule-restricted-parry: A restricted parry (unarmed against a weapon, or against an invisible foe) is worth one point for every two of OB given.
combat-rule-restricted-quarters: Fighting in a tight space: the tighter, the larger the penalty. The Restricted Quarters skill can offset it.
combat-rule-shield: The DB of the target's shield. It only covers attacks from the front, while the shield has blocks left this round.
combat-rule-shield-block: What the Shield skill adds by the declared block: the ranks when passive (the shield and the ranks together up to +50), half the skill when partial and all of it when full, the last two less the injury penalties.
combat-rule-size-difference: A smaller combatant is harder to hit: the difference between the sizes of the attacker and the target.
combat-rule-stunned-target: The target is stunned: the attacker gets a bonus.
combat-rule-style-free-ranks: The free ranks of the attacker's fighting style, added to its OB.
combat-rule-subdual: Subdual: a penalty that depends on the attack table. The hits are halved and the critical is a subdual one, never above E.
combat-rule-subdual-anatomy: The attacker does not know the anatomy of the target well.
combat-rule-subdual-damage: Subdual attack: half the hits of the table, rounded down, and a subdual critical capped at E.
combat-rule-subdual-skill: The subdual skill ({{skill}}) offsets the penalties of the maneuver ({{penalty}}), never beyond them.
combat-rule-surprised-target: The target is surprised: the attacker gets a bonus.
combat-rule-survival-instinct: Survival Instinct: a target that parries this foe with all the OB it had available gets extra DB against it.
combat-rule-trick-shot: Trick Shot: half the cover penalty is ignored.
combat-rule-two-handed-weapon: A two-handed weapon in melee: a bonus.
combat-rule-unarmed-parry: The Unarmed Parry ability of the target's fighting style makes its unarmed parry worth all the OB given.
combat-rule-uncoordinated: Uncoordinated: the attacker's pace counts as a faster one.
combat-skip-counted-by-flatfooted: The target is flatfooted: the surprise and rear bonuses already count, so this one is not added again.

docs-approach-text: Assuming familiarity with Rolemaster concepts, the application focuses on the following core ideas:
docs-concept-character: Character: A player character built using RMU design rules — attributes, skills, items and other customisations.
docs-concept-faction: Faction: A faction is a group of characters tied to a campaign. It can also represent a set of NPCs (for example, the goblins guarding a dungeon).
docs-concept-items: Items: the equipment catalog (weapons, armor, herbs, poisons and gear) that characters buy, carry and use.
docs-concept-npc: NPC: A non-player actor created either manually or derived from module content. NPCs are assigned levels, skills, equipment and hit points directly rather than through character construction rules.
docs-concept-realm: Realms: A realm defines the fictional universe for a campaign. This could be, for example, Shadow World, the official ICE universe, a realistic medieval setting without magic or Tolkien’s Middle-earth
docs-concept-spells: Spells: the spell lists and their spells, which characters learn and cast with their power points.
docs-concept-strategic-game: Strategic game: Equivalent to a campaign. It contains factions, groups, and the collection of characters and resources that make up a long-running campaign.
docs-concept-tactical-game: Tactical game: Encounters and sessions that generally involve actions and combat, played with a board and miniatures. From the tactical dashboard you declare and resolve maneuvers, movement, combat, resistance rolls and other actions.
docs-intro: This section covers the first steps for using the tool, creating a campaign, developing characters and setting up a game.
docs-official-content-text: First of all, you’ll need the <link>official ICE content</link> to play! This tool is a guide that doesn’t cover the entire game. It simply helps to streamline certain actions, such as character management and combat management.
docs-rulebooks-text: To use this assistant you should own the official rulebooks. These are available on DriveThruRPG, where you can find the full rules and game content. This assistant does not cover every option in the rules; it is intended as a practical tool to help manage characters and sessions.
docs-step-campaign: Create a campaign. Inside the realm, create a campaign and set its options, such as the experience multiplier and the board scale that turns distances into your miniatures' scale.
docs-step-characters: Add factions and characters. Group the characters of each player or band into factions and build them step by step: race, culture, profession, skills and equipment.
docs-step-realm: Choose a realm. Use one of the realms that come with the app or create your own, adjusting its races, cultures and options.
docs-step-tactical: Play an encounter. Start a tactical game from the campaign, choose who takes part and resolve each round from the combat dashboard.

finish-tactical-game-help: Finishing closes the game: it becomes read-only and its outcome can then be applied to the strategic characters. The last round's upkeep is not run.

The project is fully open source, and we welcome feedback, contributions, and suggestions from the community. You can view the source code and follow the development progress here:
force-reason-effect-help: Granted by a critical, fumble or spell: no AP and no AP penalty.
force-reason-gm-help: Game master's decision: with the AP already spent and their penalty.
force-reason-pass-through-help: A foe passes through: spends the actor's next free AP, with the penalty of the total AP.
force-reason-stray-shot-help: Second attack of a shot into a melee that missed: no AP.
force-reason-withdrawal-help: A foe withdraws: spends the actor's next free AP, with the penalty of the total AP.
force-resolution-help: Resolve the action out of turn, without waiting for its minimum action points.
free-movement-attack-pace: This actor made a free movement at {{pace}} during this attack: its pace penalty applies, unless you mark a faster pace here.
free-movement-max-run: A free movement goes up to run
free-movement-palette-help: No AP, up to run; penalizes the actions done meanwhile
free-movement-unresolved-notice: This actor has a free movement still to resolve during this action: its pace penalty will not count until it is resolved.
frenzy-attack-nearest: In frenzy: attacks the nearest creature
frenzy-dying-survives: The actor holds on until the next upkeep.
friend-invite-help: Share a link with someone you want to add as a friend. It works once and expires after 7 days.
friend-invite-once: Copy it now: it will not be shown again.
friend-invite-own-title: This is your own invitation link
friend-invite-text: If you accept, you will be friends and can share content with each other.
friend-invite-title: {{name}} has sent you a friend invitation
friend-nick-help: The exact username of the person, as it appears in their profile.
game-member-add-help: Only friends of the owner of the game can join it.
game-members-none: Nobody else plays in this game yet.
game-option-allow-saving-dev-points-help: Lets characters keep their unspent normal development points for the next level when they level up. Off by default: the points must be spent or are lost.
game-option-base-dev-points-help: Development points each character gets per level to spend on skills. More points mean more versatile characters.
game-option-board-scale-help: Converts distances to the scale of the board or map, so movements show in board units. 1 means feet as in the book.
game-option-bonus-dev-points-cap-at-crea: Applies the per-level limit of bonus development points also to the talents bought at creation, so they cannot all go into one level.
game-option-creation-bonus-dev-points-he: Extra development points the game master gives at creation, added to the race's.
game-option-experience-multiplier-help: Multiplies the experience the characters earn. Above 1 they level up faster; below 1, slower.
game-option-fatigue-multiplier-help: Multiplies the fatigue that combat actions build up. Higher values call for endurance rolls sooner; 0 turns combat fatigue off.
game-option-intense-training-help: With the game master's permission, one skill per level may take more than two ranks, each extra rank at the second cost. Not for a skill that already has ranks equal to twice the level (lores and languages are exempt from that limit). Off by default.
game-option-knack-bonus-help: Bonus each knack adds to its skill.
game-option-knack-count-help: How many skills of its profession a character can mark as knacks.
game-option-letality-help: A bonus added to every attack of the campaign. Positive values make combat deadlier; negative ones, more forgiving.
game-option-max-trait-cost-help: Most a single talent can cost at creation. Lower values keep out the most powerful talents.
game-option-open-rounds-help: An action not resolved by the end of the round carries over to the next one, keeping the action points spent. Off, unfinished actions are lost when the round ends.
game-option-power-level-preset-help: Fills the stat, knack and power point values of the power level from the table of the rules. The values stay editable; the preset is kept as a label of the game and is the default power level of the market and of enchantments.
game-option-pp-recovery-percent-help: Percent of the maximum power points recovered every 2 hours of rest, up to 4 periods a day. Talents that change the sleep only change the length of the period. Default: {{default}}%.
game-option-race-dev-points-per-level-he: Most bonus development points (of the race and the game master) a character can spend in a single level.
game-option-starting-wealth-help: Wealth category of the new characters: when a character is created in the game it gets the silver pieces of its category per starting level as gold coins in its purse. Level 0 characters get nothing. Off by default.
game-option-stat-boost-potential-help: Potential value a stat gets when a creation boost raises it to the average.
game-option-stat-boost-temporary-help: Temporary value a stat gets when a creation boost raises it to the average.
game-option-stat-creation-boosts-help: How many boosts a new character can apply to its stats: raising one to the average, raising the best ones, or extra gain rolls.
game-option-stat-creation-swaps-help: How many times a new character can exchange the values of two stats.
game-option-stat-generation-help: How the stats of a new character are generated.
game-option-stat-points-help: Budget to buy stats when they are generated by points instead of rolled.
game-option-stat-random-min-help: When stats are rolled, results below this value are rolled again. Higher values avoid very weak stats.
game-option-talent-policy-help: When and with which points talents can be bought.
game-option-talent-purchase-rules-help: Optional rules of the Character Companion: each tier of a talent needs one of its prerequisites (training and milestones are granted by the game master), a flaw must hinder the character and waits for approval when that cannot be checked, flaws taken with a talent are linked to it up to its cost, and only one loose flaw up to -20 DP is allowed. Off by default.
game-power-level-intro: How strong characters are when created: development points, how stats are generated and improved, and talents and knacks. The defaults are a heroic campaign.
game-realm-not-readable: The owner of the game can no longer read its realm: no new characters can be created and the players lose access to the realm.
game-settings-intro: Rules of the campaign: how fast characters advance, how deadly combat is and which optional rules apply. The info buttons explain each one.
game-visibility-private-help: Only the members of the game see it.
game-visibility-public-help: Anybody sees its cover and can ask to join; only members see its content.
gem-cut-fee-hint: 10 % of the new value, charged to the holder
gem-set-no-gems: This holder has no loose gems
gm-adjustment-help: Applies the result directly, without a medical action or its AP. In combat, declare a Medical action instead.
grapple-escape-help: A Feat of Strength contested with each grappler (Wrestling or Contortions), with the whole grapple penalty. The result takes its percent off the grapple. 2 to 4 AP.
grapple-feat: Feat of Strength to move away
grapple-feat-help: A grappled actor or its grappler needs a contested Feat of Strength to move away; failed, it does not move.
group-check-fear-help: Every actor of the group makes a fear RR against the fright level. A failure leaves a fear effect, the worst one kept.
group-check-info-fear-1: Called for when the group faces something terrifying or supernatural, or when the situation turns desperate.
group-check-info-fear-2: The fright level comes from the situation, the Intimidation ranks of whoever frightens them or the stat block of the creature. The higher it is, the harder to resist.
group-check-info-fear-3: Each actor makes their own RR: an open-ended roll plus their bonus against fear. Injury and fatigue penalties do not count.
group-check-info-fear-4: A present leader whom the followers recognize adds their Leadership ranks. The followers must be able to perceive the leader and heed their guidance.
group-check-info-fear-5: Passing the RR has no effect. On a failure, the wider the margin, the worse the fear state, and the actor keeps the worst one they have.
group-check-info-modifier-until-lifted: {{value}} until the game master removes it
group-check-info-morale-1: Decides whether an NPC follower accepts an order. Players decide for their own characters.
group-check-info-morale-2: An absolute maneuver of the leader: the roll, their Leadership bonus and the average RR bonus against fear of the followers.
group-check-info-morale-3: The difficulty depends on how reasonable the order seems to the follower. Whoever has no RR bonus is left out of the average.
group-check-info-morale-4: If refusing is not an option, as under threat of death, the follower obeys grudgingly even on a failure, and may go as far as sabotage on an absolute failure. The game master decides that.
group-check-info-morale-5: To direct a mount or pet towards something that frightens it, use Riding or Animal Handling instead of Leadership; on a failure, the rider takes a round to regain control. This dialog does not work that out: adjust it with the custom bonus.
group-check-info-morale-unusual: On an unmodified {{roll}}, the follower understands something else and does something different without asking.
group-check-info-no-tables: The values of the tables are only shown with Core Law access.
group-check-info-rally-1: A leader can calm whoever failed a fear check. The follower must be able to see and hear the leader.
group-check-info-rally-2: An absolute maneuver of the leader with their Leadership bonus. The book does not spell out that bonus: we use the same one as for morale.
group-check-info-rally-3: Several followers share one roll, with the modifier of the most frightened one (see the table of the Fear tab) and a penalty for how many they are.
group-check-info-rally-4: The result raises or lowers the severity of the fear of every frightened follower and applies by itself. Below the mildest state, the fear ends.
group-check-info-rally-5: Only frightened followers count: if nobody in the group is afraid, there is nothing to rally.
group-check-info-rally-unusual_one: On an unmodified {{roll}}, the leader gets fired up: {{bonus}} to their fear RR for {{count}} day and {{hits}} hits.
group-check-info-rally-unusual_other: On an unmodified {{roll}}, the leader gets fired up: {{bonus}} to their fear RR for {{count}} days and {{hits}} hits.
group-check-info-source: A summary of Core Law §14.3, in our own words. The game master has the last word.
group-check-info-state-balk: Does not advance or give chase, but defends itself if attacked.
group-check-info-state-broken: Flees at top speed, drops whatever slows it down and ignores anyone trying to stop it. If it cannot flee, it surrenders whatever the cost.
group-check-info-state-retreat: Backs away without turning from the danger. If it cannot, it surrenders when surrender costs little.
group-check-info-state-routed: Flees at a run or faster until it collapses or reaches safety. If it cannot flee, it surrenders, unless surrender means death.
group-check-morale-help: The leader rolls Leadership to have an order obeyed, with the average fear RR of the followers.
group-check-rally-help: The leader rolls Leadership to calm the frightened followers: a success lowers or removes their fear.
group-check-roll-help: Leave the roll empty and the server rolls it.
group-default-help: Pick factions or actors. With none, the group is the faction of the leader.
group-xp-help: Each chosen character gets the whole amount, not a share. The experience multiplier of the game is not applied.
group-xp-no-characters: The game has no live characters
group-xp-partial_one: {{count}} character did not get the experience
group-xp-partial_other: {{count}} characters did not get the experience
hazard-critical-alerts: The criticals without a roll are pending as alerts of the actor.
hazard-critical-pending: Pending: roll it in the alert
hazard-critical-rolls-help: Critical rolls, optional: the criticals without a roll stay as alerts of the actor.
hazard-db-help: The DB of the actor when empty
hazard-fall-control-help: Acrobatics: a success lowers the critical one level, an absolute success two, an absolute failure raises it one
hazard-fall-help: Crush attack of the size of the actor. OB: the feet fallen, less its height when it jumped on purpose. Only magical DB counts. A resolved fall-control maneuver moves the critical.
hazard-falling-object-help: Rock attack when the object is smaller than the actor, else Crush, with the size of the object (or its weight). OB: the feet it fell. The DB of the actor counts, and its shield on the Rock table.
hazard-no-fall-control: The actor has no resolved fall-control maneuver this round
hazard-severity-cap-help: A knock-back: the critical is no more severe than the one that knocked the actor back.
hazard-severity-unchanged: No size or fall control moved the critical.
hazard-temperature-help: Cold at {{cold}} °C or below, heat from {{heat}} °C: no attack roll, only the critical of cold, heat or steam. Give the temperature or, for a contact with frost or fire, the severity.
hazard-temperature-source-given: Severity given by the game master.
hazards-help: The game master resolves a fall of the actor (Crush table, OB the feet fallen, only magical DB) or an object falling on it (Rock when smaller than the actor, else Crush). The damage takes the Hit Multiplier of the size and the critical may move with the sizes and a fall control.

privacy-changes-description: This privacy policy may be updated in the future. Any changes will be reflected on this page.
privacy-contact-description: For any question about this policy or about your data, use the contact page.
privacy-controller-description: RMU Engine is a non-commercial open-source project maintained by an individual developer, who is responsible for the data described here and can be reached through the contact page.
privacy-cookies-description: Signing in uses the session cookies of the identity server (Keycloak), which are strictly necessary. Your browser keeps your preferences in its local storage: theme, language, the menu layout and which illustration the home page showed last. There are no analytics, advertising or tracking cookies.
privacy-data-collection-description: When you sign in we keep your account: display name, email, picture, the sign-in method you used (our own accounts or Google) and the date of your last sign-in. We also store what you create: realms, campaigns, factions, characters, games, images, friendships and the messages you exchange with other users.
privacy-data-storage-description: The data lives in the project's databases, on cloud infrastructure administered by the maintainer, and is kept while your account exists.
privacy-introduction-description: Which data RMU Engine stores when you sign in and use it, why, and how to ask for it to be removed.
privacy-purpose-description: Only to run the application: to identify you, keep your content under your control, let you share campaigns with your friends and show your name to the people you play with. The data is not sold, not used for advertising and not shared beyond what this page describes.
privacy-security-description: Access goes through authenticated sessions over HTTPS, and each user only reaches their own content and what others share with them.
privacy-third-party-services-description: If you choose to sign in with Google, Google authenticates you and shares your name, email and picture with us under its own privacy policy. No other third-party service receives your data.
privacy-user-rights-description: You can see and change your profile from your user page and delete your own content at any time. To get a copy of your data or to have your account deleted, write through the contact page.

home.subtitle: OpenSource Rolemaster assistant for create campaigns, manage factions, resolve tactical combats and keep your sessions organized with a clean, extendable toolset.
home.module-core-desc: Adjust game settings such as the creation of realms, races and professions, and define the general game configuration. You can use the standard RMU settings or create as many game-specific customisations as you like.
home.module-strategic-desc: Create a game with your friends using characters from a specific realm. The strategic mode allows you to create characters, equip them, and set the rules for the campaign you’ll be playing. Create your own factions and customise the characters who will be involved in future matches.
home.module-tactical-desc: Once you’ve created a campaign in tactical mode, you can battle against other players or the environment. Simply choose who’s taking part in the battle and roll the dice.
home.module-npcs-desc: Use the game's NPCs or create your own. NPCs can range from a level-one sheep to a specific level-500 character. Good luck with it.
home.module-spells-desc: Use the spells from the game's default spell lists or create your own spell lists.

spell-cast-rule-hands: Free hands to gesture ({{hands}}), read in the column of the realm ({{column}}).
spell-cast-rule-helmet: The helmet ({{helmet}}) hinders some realms more than others; this is the value of the {{column}} column.
spell-cast-rule-list-type: Own base lists are easier to cast than open, closed or other professions' lists.
spell-cast-rule-mumbler: Mumbler: -5 per tier ({{tier}}) to every Spellcasting Roll.
spell-cast-rule-overcasting: The spell is {{levels}} levels above the caster (level {{spellLevel}} against {{casterLevel}}): each level above is penalized.
spell-cast-rule-pace: The caster moves freely at {{pace}} while casting, without spending action points: the faster the pace, the larger the penalty.
spell-cast-rule-penalty-critical: Penalties of the criticals taken in this game.
spell-cast-rule-penalty-endurance: Penalty of failed endurance rolls in this game.
spell-cast-rule-penalty-fatigue: Accumulated fatigue from failed endurance rolls.
spell-cast-rule-penalty-fortitude: Fortitude takes off part of the other penalties.
spell-cast-rule-penalty-hp: Lost hit points weaken the caster.
spell-cast-rule-penalty-injury: Penalties of the injuries the caster carries.
spell-cast-rule-penalty-non-violent: The caster is in a non-violent state and acts with a penalty.
spell-cast-rule-penalty-stunned: A stunned caster casts with a penalty.
spell-cast-rule-perfected-technique: Perfected Technique: +5 per tier ({{tier}}) to the spells of the list it was taken for ({{list}}).
spell-cast-rule-preparation: Each round spent preparing the spell helps, up to a maximum.
spell-cast-rule-ranks: Ranks in the spell list: the base of the casting roll.
spell-cast-rule-realm-stat: Bonus of the stat of the caster's realm ({{realm}}).
spell-cast-rule-spell-trickery: Spell Trickery offsets the subtlety, hands and voice penalties, never more than them.
spell-cast-rule-subtlety: Casting without being noticed is harder; how much depends on the spell type ({{type}}) and the realm column ({{column}}).
spell-cast-rule-talents: A magical talent of the caster.
spell-cast-rule-transcendence: Transcendence offsets the helmet and armor penalties, never more than them.
spell-cast-rule-voice: How loud the caster speaks ({{voice}}), read in the column of the realm ({{column}}).
spell-cast-skip-armor-no-penalty: The armor ({{armor}}) does not hinder casting in the {{column}} column.
spell-cast-skip-helmet-no-penalty: The helmet ({{helmet}}) does not hinder casting in the {{column}} column.
spell-cast-skip-subtlety-not-requested: The cast is not subtle: it takes no subtlety penalty, but anyone around notices it.
spell-cast-success-rr: The spell is cast (SCR {{scr}}). It is not over yet: each target rolls a resistance roll (RR) and resists if it reaches {{scr}}.
spell-effect-critical-per-failure: severity rises with the RR failure
spell-effect-critical-same: same severity as the triggering critical
spell-effect-dispel-list: Dispels the spells of a list
spell-effect-dispel-realm: Dispels the spells of a realm
spell-effect-requires-failed-rr-help: Only applies when the target fails the resistance roll
spell-effects-invalid-json: The effects must be a JSON array of objects
spell-effects-json-help: JSON array of effects; the API checks each one when saving
spell-effects-manual: Not applied automatically yet: the game master applies them to the affected targets.
spell-failure-talent-modifier: Talents of the caster (Inglorious Failure, Graceful Recovery): {{value}}; the total is never below 1.
spell-list-not-found: The spell list {{code}} does not exist in the spells module.
spell-list-realms-help: One realm, or two for a hybrid profession
spell-outcome-all-resist: Every target resisted: the spell affects no one.
spell-outcome-failure: The spell failed: apply the spell failure result to the caster.
spell-outcome-no-rr: No resistance roll was made: decide by hand which targets are affected.
spell-outcome-no-rr-needed: The spell takes no resistance roll: its effects apply as cast.
spell-power-recycling-proposal_one: Power Recycling: {{count}} PP instead of {{base}} ({{recycled}} recycled)
spell-power-recycling-proposal_other: Power Recycling: {{count}} PP instead of {{base}} ({{recycled}} recycled)
spell-result-failure-explanation: A casting roll below 0 ({{scr}}) fails. The caster rolls on the spell failure table of its realm, adding the penalties that made the cast fail; the result says what happens and how many power points are lost.
spell-result-no-effect: No effect: the power points are lost
spell-result-no-effect-explanation: A casting roll of exactly 0 does nothing: the spell fizzles and its power points are lost.
spell-result-success-explanation: A casting roll above 0 casts the spell. Its targets may still resist it: the casting roll ({{scr}}) is what their resistance rolls must reach.
spell-rr-help: Resistance roll of each target: open-ended d100 + its RR bonus against {{realm}}, {{levelModifier}} for the caster level ({{level}}){{spellPart}}. It resists if the total reaches the SCR, {{scr}}; otherwise it is affected.
spell-rr-rule-armor: Against this realm ({{realm}}), the target's armor ({{armor}}) helps it resist.
spell-rr-rule-caster-level: Twice the caster's level ({{level}}): stronger casters are harder to resist.
spell-rr-rule-cover: Cover between caster and target ({{cover}}) helps to resist.
spell-rr-rule-helmet: Against Mentalism, a helmet ({{helmet}}) protects the mind of the target.
spell-rr-rule-iron-will: Iron Will: +5 per tier ({{tier}}) to resist mental attacks.
spell-rr-rule-range: The closer the target ({{range}}), the harder it is to resist.
spell-rr-rule-resistance: The target's resistance bonus against the realm of the spell ({{realm}}).
spell-rr-rule-spell: Some spells are easier or harder to resist by themselves.
spell-rr-rule-surprised-stunned: A surprised or stunned target resists worse.
spell-rr-rule-willing: A target that accepts the spell barely resists it.
spell-rr-skip-rr-armor-not-mentalism: Armor does not protect against Mentalism: only a helmet does.
spell-rr-skip-rr-helmet-only-mentalism: A helmet only helps against Mentalism; this spell is {{realm}}.
spell-rr-skip-rr-organic-only-essence: Organic armor only helps against Essence; this spell is {{realm}}.
spell-target-affected: {{name}} does not resist (RR {{total}} against {{required}}, short by {{failure}}): affected.
spell-target-willing: {{name}} is willing: affected without a roll.
stabilize-no-rounds-gained: The dying actor gains no rounds.
starting-wealth-rate: {{sp}} sp per level, as gold coins
stat-boosts-help: Each boost is one of: a selected stat to the average values, the highest stat to 90 or the second highest to 85 (potential +10, up to 100), or two stat gain rolls to apply on the selected stats. A swap exchanges the values of the two selected stats.
stat-generation-help-point-buy: Stats are bought with a budget of points, so every character starts on equal terms.
stat-generation-help-roll: Each stat is rolled, with rerolls below the minimum of the power level.
stat-generation-point-buy-help: Potentials are rolled (rerolls below {{min}}) and temporaries are bought with {{points}} points: each one costs its bonus.
stat-generation-roll-help: Rolls below {{min}} are rolled again. Use the boosts and swaps of the power level afterwards.
stat-level-up-help: Roll a stat gain for the selected stat. See Core Law for the full rules.
stat-point-buy-help: Choose the bonus of each temporary value: you get the highest value of the band, never above the potential.
stray-shot-attack-help: Stray shot: the attack goes at OB 0, without cover, against {{target}}, and fumbles are ignored.
stray-shot-expired: The round has ended: the stray shot is no longer available.
strenuous-failure-help: A strenuous activity failed while the injury recovered: it is active again, loses its recovery and needs a new treatment before the next recovery roll.
stun-immune-help: Any stun is a flat -25 for 1 round and does not stack.
style-ability-max-times: Already selected as many times as allowed
style-ability-no-description: No rule text has been imported for this ability.
style-ability-reminder: Reminder: the game master applies it
style-critical-effect-binding-chain: Binding Chain: Grapple critical instead of {{type}}.
style-critical-effect-lancers-knockback: Lancer's Knockback: severity lowered from {{severity}}. The foe is knocked back {{feet}}' and needs a medium Running or Acrobatics maneuver to stay standing.
style-critical-effect-leg-sweep: Leg Sweep: severity lowered from {{severity}}. The foe must beat the attack roll ({{roll}}) with a Running maneuver or fall prone.
style-critical-effect-redirect: Redirect: severity lowered from {{severity}}. Move the foe up to {{feet}}' in a direction of your choice, no more than they moved last round.
style-critical-effect-slowing-shot: Slowing Shot: severity lowered from {{severity}}. The foe's BMR drops {{feet}}' (to half at most).
style-critical-effect-weapon-breaker: Weapon Breaker: severity lowered from {{severity}}. The foe's weapon makes a breakage check at -25.
style-critical-option-help: Abilities of the active style that change the critical. Some must be decided now; the rest can wait for the critical roll.
style-equipment-not-met: Without the equipment of the style: no bonus
style-free-ranks-help: Ranks not allocated to abilities: +2 OB each, at most +10, while fighting in the style. Allocations are permanent.
subdual-adjustment: Subdual: {{base}} hits of the table → {{damage}}; critical of the table: {{critical}}.
subdual-bonus-help: Entered by the game master: it offsets the penalties of the table and of an unfamiliar anatomy, never beyond them.
surprise-declaration-help: Surprised: loses the first 2 AP, or 1 after a successful Perception. Flatfooted: no initiative and no actions this round.
tactical-game-finished-read-only: The game is finished: it is read-only.
talent-policy-flaw-points-at-creation-he: At creation talents can only be paid with the points returned by flaws, which go to their own pool instead of the normal points.
talent-policy-free-help: Talents are paid with normal development points first and then with bonus points, at creation and later.
talent-policy-help-flaw-points-at-creati: At creation, talents are paid only with the points the character's flaws give back.
talent-policy-help-free: Talents can be bought with any development points, at any level.
talent-policy-help-race-points-at-creati: New talents only at creation and only with bonus development points; later, only improvements of the ones the character has.
talent-policy-race-points-at-creation-he: At creation talents can only be paid with bonus development points; later only the talents already owned can be improved.
talent-ranks-breakdown: {{talent}} of the {{total}} ranks come from a talent
taxes-and-tolls-hint: Reference table: the game master applies them by hand.
taxes-unavailable: The taxes have not been imported.
technical-architecture: The front end is a set of micro-frontends built with <react>React</react> and <mui>MUI</mui>, loaded by a shell through Module Federation. Each domain has its own API built with <nestjs>NestJS</nestjs>, with a hexagonal layout and CQRS. A gateway serves everything under a single address.
technical-cloning-text-1: Within the <link>GitHub project</link>, we can see the set of repositories that make up the tool.
technical-cloning-text-2: As it is developed in a modular way, we won’t need to clone all the repositories—for example, if we aren’t going to use the spells or NPC modules.
technical-external-tools: The application uses the following external tools, all of which are open-source:
technical-intro: How the project is built and how to run it on your own machine.
technical-prerequisites: This guide assumes you have a basic understanding of Docker, Git, Node.js and TypeScript. If you don’t, setting up the application may prove a little tricky
technical-running-text: The rmu-platform repository holds the Docker Compose stack. With Docker installed, copy .env.example to .env and run make up: it starts the infrastructure, the APIs and the front ends. Its README explains the profiles and the rest of the commands.
technical-tool-caddy: <link>Caddy</link>: the gateway that serves the front ends and the APIs under one address.
technical-tool-kafka: <link>Apache Kafka</link>: used for asynchronous communication between modules.
technical-tool-keycloak: <link>Keycloak</link>: the identity server; it also lets users sign in with Google.
technical-tool-mongodb: <link>MongoDB</link>: a NoSQL database for storing data.
technical-tool-otel: <link>OpenTelemetry</link>: traces, metrics and logs of every service, viewed in Grafana.
